ActiveRoute.description: The route a peer is currently using for authenticated traffic.

event_id.description: Reliable message id or file batch id; never a history-list watermark.

source_id.description: Authenticated device identity, independent of the display name.

CompositeInfo.description:
Composite metadata for one history entry — **not** the entry itself (R5-05
corrected this comment, which previously described a `HistoryEntry`).

The counts are deliberately distinct, because the two UIs must not conflate them:
`representation_count` is how many formats the item carries, while `image_count`
counts image resources *and* a PNG representation. A row that says "3 formats" and
a row that says "2 images" are answering different questions, and a `native_only`
item must not be labelled as several cross-platform formats at all.

formats.description:
Format names present in the item, for display.

**Present is not the same as restorable.** A menu built from this alone can offer
an action the server will refuse, which is exactly what R5-04 forbids; build the
menu from [`Self::restorable_formats`] instead.

image_count.description: How many images the item carries: resources plus a PNG representation.

native_only.description:
The item was captured as a platform-native shape and can only be replayed on
that platform; the UIs must not offer cross-platform formats for it.

representation_count.description: How many representations (formats) the item carries.

restorable_formats.description:
The single-format restore actions the server will actually accept, in a stable
order. This is what a menu must be built from.

withheld_formats.description:
Formats that are present but deliberately not offered, with the stable code the
UI localises instead of inventing its own explanation.

ConnectionInterface.description: The transport a peer route uses.

FavoriteMutation.description: Result of changing the favorite state of a logical history item.

size_bytes.description:
**Logical size**: the size of the captured content itself, independent of how
it is stored. For a composite item this is the sum of its parts' logical sizes,
so it stays meaningful even when the bytes live outside the database.

Not to be confused with the two other sizes in this API: the **external
physical size** (what a part actually occupies on disk once externalised) and
the **preview binary size** (`PreviewMetadata::size_bytes`, which describes the
preview artefact being transferred, not the stored item).

notification_dropped_total.description:
How many notifications were evicted from the bounded buffer since this daemon
started, for diagnostics and trend.

notification_earliest_available_id.description:
Oldest notification id still readable. A client whose cursor is below
`notification_earliest_available_id - 1` has missed events that can no longer
be read and must re-read a full snapshot instead of trusting its cursor.

service_instance.description:
Identifies this daemon process. A changed value means the daemon restarted, so
any cursor the client kept refers to a previous instance.

PairingFailureKind.description:
Finite classification of a pairing failure.

The set is deliberately small: a failure that cannot be attributed to one
of these buckets stays [`PairingFailureKind::Unknown`] rather than being
guessed from text.

failure_kind.description:
Finite classification of the failure that produced `error`, when the
producer knew one. Omitted entirely when there is no classification, so
an older shell model that never heard of the field still decodes.

PeerCandidate.description:
One reachable route for a peer, with the health fields the health monitor
derives. Legacy serialized candidates without `online`/`status` keep
working through serde defaults.

rtt_capable.description:
Whether latency can be measured over this route. LAN/Tailscale routes
are always testable; Iroh routes require the peer to have advertised
RTT support and to have been rediscovered.

PeerRouteSnapshot.description:
One serialized route row of the peer snapshot, shared by both platform
JSON APIs (mirrored by the Swift `Route` DTO and the React `PeerRoute`
interface). Field names are part of the wire contract; the drift check
compares this struct's fields against the contract lists.

PeerSnapshot.description:
A discovered or remembered peer device. This is the unified cross-platform
shape: macOS and Windows previously carried slightly different field sets
(Windows lacked `current_address` and `status`), which made shared
directory logic impossible and let the JSON contracts drift.

PeerStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a discovered peer.

Projected health state is consistent when a peer or candidate is `online`
iff its status is
[`PeerStatus::Connected`], [`PeerStatus::Online`], or
[`PeerStatus::Confirming`]. [`PeerInfo::is_consistent`] and
[`PeerCandidate::is_consistent`] check this. Legacy wire data can contain
older field combinations; the health projection (`apply_peer_health`)
normalizes both fields before exposing a fresh snapshot.

PreviewBatchNavigation.description:
Ordered navigation state for the current item in a file batch.

`item_index` is zero-based and `item_count` is derived from the rows that
are actually present. This keeps incomplete batches navigable without
trusting stale `batch_total` metadata.

PreviewErrorCode.description: Stable error categories exposed by platform preview adapters.

PreviewErrorInfo.description:
Stable, transport-neutral preview failure exposed by platform adapters.

Platform code serializes this value using its native IPC framing. Keeping
retryability and size details here prevents Windows and macOS from
interpreting free-form error messages differently.

StableErrorCode.description:
Stable local-IPC error categories. Deserializers deliberately map future
categories to `internal_error` so an older UI never crashes or guesses a
retry policy for an error it does not understand.

StableErrorDetailClass.description:
Coarse, non-sensitive context for localizing an error. These values never
contain clipboard data, file paths, peer identities, keys, or tokens.

StableErrorEnvelope.description:
Versioned error returned to clients that explicitly opt in to the stable
local contract. The legacy message is used only for classification and is
never copied into this envelope.

id.description:
Stable identity of this warning, so a consumer can read it without consuming it
and then acknowledge exactly the one it showed.

WithheldRestoreFormat.description: A restore format that is present on the item but that the server will refuse.

format.description: The format name, matching one entry of `CompositeInfo::formats`.
